A1.justification: Both PDFs describe G4Splat with the same authors and core framework. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Replica, ScanNet++ and DeepBlending, alongside ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary single-view, dense-view and varying-view results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds Mip-NeRF 360 evaluations and experiments using ViewCrafter as an alternative generative prior.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the reported non-planar depth rule: v1 generally uses aligned monocular depth, whereas v2 retains MAtCha depth in input-visible non-planar regions and uses monocular depth for unobserved regions. This is a localized procedural revision. The first-visible-view color-supervision rule added to the main text already appeared in v1 Appendix C.3.

E1.justification: v2 adds nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes, including five outdoor, non-Manhattan and less structured scenes. This substantially extends systematic evaluation of a method motivated by planar structures. The three original benchmarks and single-view, unposed-video and dense-view examples are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. The new benchmark and prior-comparison tables reuse existing baselines, including MAtCha, GenFusion, Difix3D+, GuidedVD and See3D. ViewCrafter is evaluated as a component variant of G4Splat; newly cited geometry-prior methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a nine-input-view protocol for Mip-NeRF 360, reporting rendering metrics only because ground-truth meshes are unavailable, and adds an alternative-generative-prior configuration. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged. Original sampling and test-split details expanded in Section 4.1 were already documented in v1 Appendix C.5.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a sensitivity comparison between ViewCrafter and See3D within G4Splat, supported by Table A2 and Figure A4. The original component ablations, varying-view analysis, consistency examples and failure cases are retained. Figure A6 primarily redisplays existing examples with visibility annotations.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical tests. The additional tables retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and A3 add aggregate and per-scene Mip-NeRF 360 results: G4Splat reports mean PSNR 18.66, SSIM 0.515 and LPIPS 0.371, leading the reported means but not every scene and metric. Table A2 adds the ViewCrafter variant, including CD 7.95 and PSNR 22.08. Original benchmark, ablation, runtime and varying-view values are unchanged; these additions do not establish same-setting v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: The plane-model assumptions, equations 1–6, Appendix equations A1–A14 and reconstruction-metric definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced; the non-planar supervision revision concerns the algorithm's choice of depth source.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims about geometry-guided generative reconstruction, improved observed and unobserved regions, and support for single-view and unposed inputs. Adding Mip-NeRF 360 broadens supporting evidence without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds a substantive explanation attributing reliability in less structured scenes to preserving base-model supervision in visible non-planar regions and using monocular depth elsewhere. Appendix C.4 interprets the ViewCrafter experiment as effectiveness with another generative prior. Existing limitations concerning color inconsistency, severe occlusion and plane representations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that plane-extraction normal maps can come from depth-map gradients or a monocular predictor, citing StableNormal; v1 leaves their source unspecified. Hardware, three generative loops, ten additional views per loop, 7000-iteration stages and the project-page address are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds acknowledgment of 3D geometry-prior approaches through Spurfies, CUPID and ReconViaGen. Mip-NeRF 360 and StableNormal references are also added. The broader positioning relative to sparse-view, generative-prior and plane-based reconstruction remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds a method-section roadmap, expands settings and non-planar supervision explanations, and updates the conference header and author-role information. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact; this is localized editing rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: The empirical displays expand substantially: Figure 4 gains Mip-NeRF 360 examples; Tables 2, A2 and A3 and Figures A4 and A7 present added evaluations. Figure A6 redisplays existing examples with golden visibility-mask overlays. Existing failure cases, metric definitions and supplementary comparisons are retained under new numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: The Mip-NeRF 360 results in Tables 2/A3 and alternative-prior comparison in Table A2 strengthen support for generalization beyond structured scenes and a single generative model. Clearer supervision descriptions and visibility annotations also improve interpretability. These extend an already extensive evaluation: the added benchmark lacks quantitative geometry validation, and the revised non-planar depth rule is not separately evaluated, limiting the strength of the improvement.
